Photograph: Yui Mok/PA View image in fullscreen A family lay flowers on the beach at Shoreham-by-Sea, where four members of the El-Khawas family died after getting in trouble in the sea. Photograph: Yui Mok/PA West Sussex Girl, 6, dies three days after Shoreham sea incident that killed parents and sister Saja El-Khawas had been in critical condition after being pulled from sea in West Sussex Harry Cockburn Fri 21 Aug 2026 18.50 EDT Last modified on Fri 21 Aug 2026 19.09 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A six-year-old girl has died in hospital three days after being pulled from the sea off Shoreham in West Sussex , in an incident that also killed her mother, father and sister. Saja El-Khawas died on Friday after the deaths of her sister Sara El-Khawas, 14, and her parents Hassan El-Khawas, 55, and Zeina Alayn, 37, on Tuesday. Saja had been in hospital in a critical condition since the incident. Police, paramedics, coastguard crews and a lifeboat attended the scene at Shoreham Fort early on Tuesday afternoon after a report of four people in difficulty in the water. In a statement, Sussex police said: “It is understood the family travelled down from their home in London to visit Shoreham, and entered the water from the beach at Shoreham Fort around 2pm on Tuesday afternoon, before getting into trouble. “The investigation into the incident remains open, but following review of CCTV footage and initial witness accounts, the current hypothesis is that this was a tragic accident, with no third-party involvement.” Her identity and death were confirmed in a legal notice from solicitors acting on behalf of Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS foundation trust, as well as the Palestinian Forum in Britain. The Palestinian embassy previously confirmed her father was a British citizen of Palestinian descent. Sussex police said the family’s next of kin “are aware and continue to receive the full support of our officers during this unimaginably difficult time”. Ch Supt James Collis said: “This heartbreaking update is one we all feared in the aftermath of Tuesday’s tragic events. “I cannot imagine the devastation felt by the wider family of Hassan, Zeina, Sara and Saja after this loss. On behalf of everyone at Sussex police, I extend our thoughts and heartfelt condolences. “The impact of this tragedy has been felt across the country, and I know the Shoreham community, emergency responders and all involved will continue to be affected for a long time to come.” “I would like to thank all of the public who have shared their sympathies and kind words, and once again ask for the victims’ family and loved ones to be left to grieve in privacy.” Explore more on these topics West Sussex news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Two men accused of rape and sexual assault following an attack on two girls at a Norfolk beach are to appear in court this month. Madalin Ilinca has been charged with one count of rape, one count of sexual assault, and one offence of sexual assault by penetration. Dawid Wlach is accused of rape, oral rape, assault by penetration, and sexual assault. It comes after two teenage girls - neither of whom can be identified for legal reasons - reported they had been raped on Great Yarmouth's South Beach on May 16. Ilinca, a 34-year-old Romanian national, of Suffolk Place, Yarmouth, and Wlach, a 35-year-old Polish national, of Dover Court in Caister, are set to appear at Norwich Crown Court on August 25. Norwich Crown Court (Image: Peter Walsh, Newsquest) At a plea and trial preparation hearing (PTPH) held last month, Ilinca denied the rape and sexual assault of one girl and an offence of assault by penetration against another. Wlach has not yet entered any pleas as he was appearing at Norwich Magistrates Court on July 28 - the same day as his co-defendant's PTPH hearing. A potential trial date has been fixed for December 7. Court Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading...
